title: Why orchestrate: what Compose does not solve

videos.script: Ana's shop runs on one machine, with Docker Compose. One file, one command, and the site answers. {{compose}} This course starts from that file, because it is a good one. Compose restarts a process that crashes. It keeps a network and the volumes. For one machine, that is enough. {{restart}} The trouble is at the edges of the machine. A second copy cannot take the same port. An update stops the old container before the new one answers. And when the machine dies, everything on it dies with it. {{edges}} You will measure two of those edges in this lesson. One costs a refused command. The other costs twelve requests that got no answer. {{measure}} Then you will name what an orchestrator adds: several machines, a desired state written down, and a program that keeps comparing the two. {{orchestrator}}
